podcast.body: This song is featured on the "Temple of the Dog" album, released in 1990. The album was a collaborative effort recorded by members of Mother Love Bone and Soundgarden as a memorial to Mother Love Bone's late singer, Andrew Wood. "Temple of the Dog and Hunger Strike from their one and only album from 1990."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unprompted Eddie Vedder Duet
podcast.body: During the recording of this song, while Chris Cornell was laying down vocals, Eddie Vedder spontaneously picked up a microphone and began singing the low harmonies without being asked. This impromptu contribution solidified the legendary duet between the two future rock giants, recorded at a time when neither Soundgarden nor the nascent Pearl Jam were widely known. "But in the midst of Chris recording the vocals for the song that we're about to hear, Eddie just picked up a mic and started singing the low parts. Nobody really asked him to do it, he just kind of did it."

podcast.body: This song from the "Temple of the Dog" album became a top 10 hit at both album and modern rock radio, contributing significantly to the album's belated platinum success. "Temple of the Dog's self-titled one-off album even generated a top 10 hit at both album and modern rock radio called Hunger Strike."
